key_insight: A physics-guided generative AI pipeline can design 3D porous structures to match target porosity and directional permeability by combining a property-aware VAE, conditional latent diffusion, and a differentiable structure-to-property surrogate.
clinical_relevance: For biomedical scaffolds and other porous implants, this approach could help engineers rapidly tailor microstructure to support desired transport and mechanical performance before fabrication.
method: Trains a property-aware variational autoencoder to learn a compact latent design space for porous media.
Uses a conditional latent diffusion model to generate structures from target porosity and permeability values.
Applies an independently trained differentiable surrogate to provide property feedback during denoising and decoding.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved target-property matching, directional permeability control, and property correlation on both procedurally generated structures and real micro-CT porous-media datasets.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and representativeness of the training data, and generated designs still need simulation or experimental validation before practical use.
paper_title: Physics-Guided Generative AI for Property-Targeted 3D Porous Media Design
